title: Investigation of the refractive visual potential in a university patient population with regard to autorefractive visual acuity, spectacle visual acuity and best corrected visual acuity
summary: In ophthalmology, it is important to achieve the best possible vision in the long term. In addition to eye diseases, individual visual acuity plays a decisive role. Uncorrected visual impairments can affect vision. This study examines the satisfaction of patients with their spectacle care in a university medical setting. It examines variations between different vision tests and spectacle corrections and their impact on patients' vision and subjective well-being.

interventions.name: Participants' objective refraction and visual acuity are measured on an autorefractometer, current spectacle values are measured and the Visual Function Questionnaire (NEI-VFQ) is carried out
In the second arm, the visual acuity in free room is also measured with the objective refraction, the refraction values of the spectacles and after subjective adjustment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Outpatient examination or therapy at the Eye Clinic of Hannover Medical School
Exclusion criteria:
Visual acuity less than or equal to 0.3 cc
Persons incapable of giving consent
Any acute pathology that could have led to an acute change in refraction
within the last 6 months before the start of the study
